original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Spokesperson for Indian Ocean island nation says they will try to recover explorers in next couple of days

Rescuers have located the bodies of four Italian divers deep inside an underwater cave in an atoll in the Maldives, four days after they were reported missing.

Searches had resumed after being suspended following the death of a local military diver during a perilous mission to try to reach them.

The government of the Indian Ocean island nation confirmed on Monday the bodies were spotted in the innermost part of the cave by three Finnish diving experts, supported by the Maldives police and the military.

“As was previously thought, the four bodies were found inside the cave, not only inside the cave but well inside the cave into the third segment of the cave, which is the largest part,” said Ahmed Shaam, a Maldives government spokesperson.

He said the four were found “pretty much together”.

“The plan is they will try and recover two bodies tomorrow and possibly the other two the following day,” Shaam said in a voice clip sent to the media.

The body of a fifth Italian, a diving instructor, was found earlier outside the cave. The five were exploring a cave at a depth of about 50 metres (160ft) in Vaavu Atoll on Thursday, according to Italy’s foreign ministry. The recreational diving limit in the Maldives is 30 metres.

Three Finnish divers, experts in deep and cave diving arrived in the Maldives on Sunday.

The Maldives presidential spokesperson, Mohamed Hussain Shareef, said earlier that the search was suspended after Mohamed Mahudhee, a member of the Maldives National Defence Force, died of underwater decompression sickness after being transferred to a hospital in the capital on Saturday.

Rough weather has repeatedly hampered rescue efforts.

Initial teams had already dived to identify and mark the entrance to the cave system where the Italians disappeared. The cause of the deaths remains under investigation.

Searches had resumed on Monday after being suspended following the death of a local military diver during a perilous mission to try to reach them.

The government of the Indian Ocean island nation confirmed the bodies were spotted in the innermost part of the cave by three Finnish diving experts, supported by the Maldives police and the military.

"As was previously thought, the four bodies were found inside the cave, not only inside the cave but well inside the cave into the third segment of the cave, which is the largest part," said Ahmed Shaam, a Maldives government spokesman.

He said the four were found "pretty much together."

"The plan is they will try and recover two bodies tomorrow and possibly the other two the following day," Shaam said in a voice clip sent to the media.

The body of a fifth Italian - a diving instructor - was found earlier outside the cave. The five were exploring a cave at a depth of about 160 feet in Vaavu Atoll on Thursday, according to Italy's Foreign Ministry. The recreational diving limit in the Maldives is 30 meters (98 feet).

Three Finnish divers, experts in deep and cave diving arrived in the Maldives on Sunday.

Maldives presidential spokesperson Mohamed Hussain Shareef said earlier that the search was suspended after Mohamed Mahudhee, a member of the Maldivian National Defense Force, died of underwater decompression sickness after being transferred to a hospital in the capital on Saturday.

The victims have been identified as Monica Montefalcone, an associate professor of ecology at the University of Genoa; her daughter, Giorgia Sommacal; marine biologist Federico Gualtieri; researcher Muriel Oddenino; and diving instructor Gianluca Benedetti, according to the Maldivian government.

Benedetti's body was the one recovered on Thursday from near the mouth of the cave.

Montefalcone and Oddenino were in the Maldives on an official scientific mission to monitor marine environments and study the effects of climate change on tropical biodiversity, the University of Genoa said in a statement Friday. payload.title: Neljän italialaissukeltajan ruumiit paikannettiin Malediivien vedenalaisesta luolasta
payload.summary: Pelastajat ovat paikantaneet neljän italialaissukeltajan ruumiit syvältä vedenalaisesta luolasta Malediiveilla. Löydön tekivät suomalaiset sukellusasiantuntijat poliisin ja armeijan tukemassa vaarallisessa operaatiossa.
payload.content:
Pelastajat ovat paikantaneet neljän italialaissukeltajan ruumiit syvältä vedenalaisesta luolasta Malediivien atollilla. Viranomaisten mukaan ruumiit havaittiin maanantaina luolan sisimmässä osassa, neljä päivää sen jälkeen kun sukeltajat ilmoitettiin kadonneiksi torstaina.

## Löytö tehtiin luolan sisimmässä osassa

Malediivien hallitus kertoi, että ruumiit havaitsivat kolme suomalaista sukellusasiantuntijaa. Heidän työtään tukivat Malediivien poliisi ja maan asevoimat. Hallituksen edustaja Ahmed Shaam sanoi, että ruumiit olivat luolassa syvällä, sen kolmannessa osassa, jota hän kuvasi luolan suurimmaksi alueeksi.

Viranomaisten mukaan tavoitteena on yrittää nostaa ruumiit seuraavien päivien aikana. Tehtävää pidetään poikkeuksellisen vaarallisena, koska etsittävät ovat vedenalaisen luolaston sisällä, kaukana helposta pääsystä ja paluureitistä.

Italian ulkoministeriö vahvisti maanantaina, että pelastajat olivat paikantaneet neljän italialaisen ruumiit. Lähdeaineiston mukaan katoaminen liittyi syväsukellukseen, jota tutkijat pitävät luvattomana ja joka ylitti Malediivien virkistyssukellukselle asetetun rajan.

## Etsintä keskeytyi kuolemantapauksen jälkeen

Etsintöjä oli aiemmin keskeytetty lauantaina sen jälkeen, kun Malediivien asevoimien sukeltaja kuoli yrittäessään päästä kadonneiden luo. Malediivien presidentin edustajan mukaan sotilassukeltaja Mohamed Mahdi menehtyi sukeltajantaudin seurauksena vaarallisen tehtävän aikana.

Kadonneiden joukossa oli merentutkimuksen ja sukelluksen kokeneita ammattilaisia. Malediivien hallituksen mukaan ryhmään kuuluivat muun muassa Genovan yliopiston ekologian professori Monica Montefalcone, hänen tyttärensä Giorgia Sommacal, meribiologi Federico Gualtieri, tutkija Muriel Oddenino ja sukelluskouluttaja Gianluca Benedetti.

## Seuraavaksi arvioidaan nostoyritystä

Pelastusoperaation seuraava vaihe on ruumiiden nostaminen luolasta, jos olosuhteet sen sallivat. Viranomaiset eivät ole antaneet tarkkaa aikataulua, mutta hallituksen edustajan mukaan työtä pyritään jatkamaan lähipäivinä. Tapaus on samalla korostanut sitä, miten vaikeaksi syvällä luolassa tapahtuva etsintä voi muuttua myös kokeneille sukeltajille ja heitä auttaville viranomaisille.
